learningObjectives: Assay a kinematic construction by naming its represented objects, domain, structures, observables, and reconstruction map.
Diagnose coordinate, branch, and category failures in worked examples.
Separate tensor-network, OPE-block, and integral-geometric evidence by their inputs and conclusions.
Formulate an open question as a missing map, inaccessible region, or failed test rather than as an unsupported analogy.
definitions: Construction assay: a check of represented objects, coordinate domain, imposed structures, source observables, and reconstruction maps.
Coordinate failure: loss or duplication caused by omitted orientation, quotient, or domain information.
Branch failure: loss of relevant solutions when several geodesics or phases share coarse labels.
Category failure: conflation of relations belonging to different represented spaces.
Reconstruction domain: the class of objects or regions that supplied observables can determine.
Open reconstruction question: a precisely stated missing map or identifiability test.
notebookPrompt: Create a culminating mathematical cinematic titled ‘Worked constructions, failure cases, and open questions.’ Build a five-stage assay that checks represented objects, coordinate domain and identifications, kinematic relations or measure, source observables, and the reconstruction theorem. Run the vacuum interval/geodesic construction through it successfully. Then demonstrate coordinate failure from omitted orientation, branch failure from multiple geodesics or entropy phases, and category failure from treating a discretized space of geodesics as a lattice of bulk points. Compare what integral geometry, OPE blocks, and tensor networks separately warrant. In a final negative control, feed an arbitrary pairwise-relation dataset into the assay and stop visibly at the first missing hypothesis rather than inventing a de Sitter geometry. End with several open questions phrased as missing maps or tests and preserve all semiclassical, state, and model limits.
humanFrame: This is a methods lesson: success means knowing where to stop an inference. Reuse visual elements from earlier lessons so every failure can be located at a specific construction stage.
assessment: Given one proposed ‘kinematic space’ analogy, complete the five-stage assay, identify at least one coordinate, branch, or category failure, and rewrite one vague frontier claim as a testable open reconstruction question.
